scenes.title: Jacquard loom
scenes.blurb: Punched cards drive a thread-level loom; paint the point paper, punch the cards.
scenes.fits: textiles, punched cards, stored programs, pattern, weaving

scenes.title: Cabaret Voltaire cut-up
scenes.blurb: A letterpress bill composes chance poems from a bag of cut-up newsprint.
scenes.fits: chance, collage, typography, avant-garde, performance, sound poetry

scenes.title: Phosphor oscilloscope
scenes.blurb: A beam traces two electrical waves; tune the knobs, hear the ratio, expose a photograph.
scenes.fits: analog electronics, oscilloscopes, Lissajous figures, light, early electronic art, photography of screens

scenes.title: Pen plotter and teletype
scenes.blurb: A 1960s plotter draws original algorithmic studies set by a switch register.
scenes.fits: mainframe computer art, plotters, algorithmic drawing, 1960s computer graphics, exhibitions of computer art

scenes.title: Analog video synthesizer
scenes.blurb: Patch cords route video through processors and camera feedback.
scenes.fits: video art, video synthesis, feedback, image processing, analog signal art

scenes.title: Commodore 64 and 10 PRINT
scenes.blurb: A home computer boots, runs the 10 PRINT maze and turns it into a game.
scenes.fits: home computers, 8-bit, video games, demoscene, BASIC, personal computing

scenes.title: 1995 desktop and net.art
scenes.blurb: A dial-up desktop where every link spawns a generated net.art page.
scenes.fits: the web, net.art, HTML, browsers, mailing lists, hypertext, online communities

scenes.title: Processing sketchbook
scenes.blurb: Live code: drag any number and the sketch changes.
scenes.fits: creative coding, software tools, open source, programming for artists, frameworks

scenes.title: GAN training live
scenes.blurb: A generator and discriminator train in the browser on data you draw.
scenes.fits: machine learning, neural networks, GANs, AI art, training data

scenes.title: On-chain long-form mint
scenes.blurb: A simulated chain mints an original algorithm from token hashes.
scenes.fits: blockchain, NFTs, long-form generative art, smart contracts, minting platforms

scenes.title: Firelit cave engraving
scenes.blurb: Torchlight on a rock wall; ochre hatching engraved by a symmetry rule, as at Blombos.
scenes.fits: prehistoric pattern, symmetry, rule-based marks, ancient ornament, tiling
scenes.brief: A dark cave wall lit by a hand-held torch (the pointer): flickering firelight, rock texture, ochre pigment. A symmetry-based hatching rule engraves cross-hatched bands mark by mark; the viewer scratches strokes and the rule completes them symmetrically. Other prehistoric and ancient pattern systems (tiling, meander, basketry) can appear as the rule changes.

scenes.title: Musical dice game
scenes.blurb: Roll two dice per bar to assemble a minuet from pre-composed measures, then hear it on a harpsichord.
scenes.fits: chance music, aleatoric composition, combinatorics, games, early algorithmic music
scenes.brief: An 18th-century table: two dice, a lookup table of numbered measures, engraved score paper. Roll (click or shake) and the dice pick a measure for each bar; the measure is engraved onto the staff; the finished minuet plays on a synthesized harpsichord. Measures are ORIGINAL (composed in code in the galant style), never copied from a historical table. Show how many distinct minuets the table allows.

scenes.title: Analytical Engine
scenes.blurb: Brass columns of number wheels compute Bernoulli numbers step by step, as Lovelace planned in Note G.
scenes.fits: mechanical computation, Babbage, Lovelace, algorithms, early computing
scenes.brief: A brass-and-steel mechanism: the Store (columns of decimal wheels) and the Mill, card chains for operations and variables. It runs a Bernoulli-number computation, wheels turning and carries rippling, with a live table of operations in the style of Note G (the structure of the method, computed correctly, not a facsimile of her table). The viewer can step, run faster, or change which Bernoulli number to compute.
scenes.dropped: Peter, 23 Sep: hard to grasp, and the Analytical Engine was never built, so a working scene shows something that never existed.

scenes.title: Camera obscura heliograph
scenes.blurb: A camera obscura exposes a bitumen plate for hours; the sun crosses the courtyard as the image slowly forms.
scenes.fits: photography, light-sensitive processes, long exposure, optics, image capture
scenes.brief: Inside a camera obscura: an inverted, dim view of rooftops and a courtyard (drawn procedurally) projected onto a plate. Time compresses: the sun moves across the sky, shadows fall on both sides, and the bitumen image hardens gradually. The viewer can change the exposure length and see the image form, then wash the plate to reveal it.

scenes.title: Suprematist composition
scenes.blurb: Squares, bars and circles float in white space and settle into non-objective compositions.
scenes.fits: Suprematism, Constructivism, abstraction, geometric composition, avant-garde painting, Bauhaus
scenes.brief: Coloured planes (black, red, ochre, blue) drift on white canvas in weightless space and settle into balanced asymmetric compositions by simple rules (tension, diagonal thrust, overlap). The viewer drags forms and the system rebalances. Original compositions only; never recreate a specific painting. A corner-hung canvas nods to the 1915 exhibition.

scenes.title: Cybernetic tortoises
scenes.blurb: Two light-seeking robot tortoises wander, steer by feedback and find their way home to the charging hutch.
scenes.fits: cybernetics, feedback, robotics, behaviour, homeostasis, control systems
scenes.brief: A dim room seen from above. Two small three-wheeled robots with a scanning photocell and a headlamp wander, approach moderate light, avoid bright light, bump and back off, and return to a lit hutch as their batteries drain; they respond to each other lamps. The viewer moves a light (pointer) and places obstacles. Original simulation of the behaviour, labelled as such.

scenes.title: Information theory teletype
scenes.blurb: A teletype prints text approximating English by letter and word statistics, from random letters to near-sentences.
scenes.fits: information theory, Markov chains, text generation, statistics of language, communication
scenes.brief: A teletype and a small dial of orders: zero-order random letters, first-order letter frequencies, second and third-order letter chains, then word-level chains. The machine prints samples generated live from statistics of a public-domain English text; a noisy-channel toggle shows bits flipping. The viewer turns the order dial and feeds their own text.

scenes.title: I Ching chance score
scenes.blurb: Three coins thrown six times build a hexagram that picks the next event in a chance score.
scenes.fits: chance operations, indeterminacy, Neo-Dada, Fluxus, happenings, experimental music
scenes.brief: Three coins tossed six times build a hexagram line by line; the hexagram number indexes a chart of sounds, durations and dynamics; a graphic score grows across a long sheet and plays (prepared-piano-like percussive synthesis, silences). The viewer tosses the coins. Original chart and sounds; never a reproduction of a real score.

scenes.title: Ferranti love letters
scenes.blurb: An early stored-program computer composes love letters from a random word list on its teleprinter.
scenes.fits: computer text, generative poetry, early computing, combinatorial literature
scenes.brief: A 1950s machine room: a monitor tube showing the memory as a dot raster, a hooter, a teleprinter printing letters in the known template (salutation, sentences from adjective/noun/adverb/verb slots, signature). Use an ORIGINAL vocabulary in the same grammatical template, clearly labelled as a reconstruction of the method. The viewer presses to compose and can add words.

scenes.title: Random-dot stereogram
scenes.blurb: A field of random dots hides a shape that only appears in depth; cross your eyes and it floats.
scenes.fits: perception, depth, optical art, computer graphics research, Bell Labs, Op Art
scenes.brief: A live random-dot stereogram pair (and an anaglyph toggle for red-cyan glasses) generated from a hidden depth map that the viewer can draw or select (shapes, letters, a rotating solid). Includes a gentle guide for free-fusing (converge to see the shape), and a reveal slider that shows the hidden map. Dots regenerate each frame option (dynamic RDS).

scenes.title: Colour copier generative print
scenes.blurb: Objects on the glass, a sweeping light bar, colour controls: the copier makes a generative print each pass.
scenes.fits: generative systems, copy art, electrostatic printing, participatory art, women artists, 1970s art and technology
scenes.brief: Top view of a 1970s colour copier: the lid opens, the viewer drags objects (a hand, leaves, lace, type, their own drawing) onto the glass, the light bar sweeps, and a print slides out with the colour separation, registration shifts and toner grain of electrostatic colour copying; moving objects during the sweep smears them. Colour controls change each pass. Keep machine generic, no brand.

scenes.title: 1-bit paint program
scenes.blurb: A 1984 black-and-white paint program: patterns, fat bits, spray can and a generative brush.
scenes.fits: personal computers, bitmap graphics, graphical user interface, 1984, digital drawing
scenes.brief: A 512x342 one-bit screen in a generic 1984 desktop: tool palette, 38 fill patterns, fat bits zoom, spray can, lasso, and a generative brush that repeats and mirrors strokes. It opens mid-drawing with an attract demo; the viewer paints. No Apple branding, no copied icons.

scenes.title: Fractal flame screensaver
scenes.blurb: Networked screensavers render fractal flames that viewers vote on and breed into new generations.
scenes.fits: fractals, artificial life, genetic algorithms, distributed computing, screensavers
scenes.brief: A GPU fractal-flame renderer (iterated function systems with nonlinear variations, log-density tone mapping, colour palettes) morphing between genomes. A small 1999-style panel shows a simulated network of clients rendering frames; the viewer votes up or down and breeds two genomes into offspring. Original genomes only; labelled simulation of the network.

scenes.title: Evolved virtual creatures
scenes.blurb: Block-bodied creatures evolve their bodies and brains to swim, generation by generation.
scenes.fits: artificial life, evolution, genetic algorithms, physics simulation, 1990s computer graphics
scenes.brief: A 2D (or simple 3D-look) water world where jointed block creatures with small neural controllers are evaluated for swimming distance; the best reproduce with mutation and crossover; generations advance live with a fitness graph. The viewer can pick parents, change the task (swim, follow a light). Original implementation of the method, labelled as such.

scenes.title: Proof-of-work mining
scenes.blurb: Nonces race through a hash function until one falls under the target, and a block is sealed.
scenes.fits: cryptography, hashing, proof of work, blockchains, peer-to-peer networks
scenes.brief: A real SHA-256 computed live in the browser: nonce counter spinning, hashes streaming, leading-zero target line; when a hash beats the target a block is sealed and chained with its previous hash; difficulty adjusts. The viewer changes difficulty, edits a past transaction and watches the chain break. Labelled simulation, no real network.

scenes.title: Diffusion denoising
scenes.blurb: Noise is reversed step by step into data by a small network trained live in the browser.
scenes.fits: diffusion models, denoising, text-to-image, generative AI, thermodynamics
scenes.brief: A real small diffusion model on 2D data (like the GAN scene but visually distinct): forward process scatters points into Gaussian noise; the trained denoiser reverses it step by step with trajectories drawn as flowing curves; the viewer draws data, scrubs the timestep, and watches samples crystallise. Show the noise schedule. Honest: trained live, no pretrained model.

scenes.title: Vector graphics language
scenes.blurb: An artist types commands and a vector display draws and animates them at once, the way GRASS and Zgrass let artists perform graphics.
scenes.fits: graphics programming languages, vector displays, real-time animation, performance with computers, 1970s art labs
scenes.brief: A 1970s vector-display workstation: a green or white vector CRT beside a terminal. The viewer types short commands (or picks from a menu of ready phrases) in an original GRASS-like language: draw, rotate, scale, repeat, colorize; the display redraws live with vector glow, flicker and persistence. Attract mode runs a performer typing a sequence that builds and animates a figure. Label the language as an original reconstruction in the spirit of the era.

scenes.title: 3D rendering pipeline
scenes.blurb: One object passes from wireframe to flat, Gouraud and Phong shading, then ray-traced reflections, as 1970s and 80s graphics research added each step.
scenes.fits: 3D computer graphics, rendering, shading models, ray tracing, computer animation, graphics research
scenes.brief: The Utah teapot (the classic public test model, built from its public Bezier patch data or approximated by an original surface) on a studio floor, with a stepper: wireframe, hidden lines, flat, Gouraud, Phong, textured, ray-traced reflections and soft shadows. Each step names the technique and the decade. The viewer orbits the camera, moves the light and scrubs the pipeline. Real-time GPU approximations, labelled honestly.

scenes.title: Mandelbrot and chaos
scenes.blurb: An endless zoom into the Mandelbrot set beside a Lorenz attractor tracing its butterfly: simple rules, infinite detail.
scenes.fits: fractals, chaos theory, mathematics in art, iteration, self-similarity
scenes.brief: A deep-zoom Mandelbrot renderer on the GPU (smooth colouring) with a Lorenz attractor drawn in a side panel; the viewer clicks to zoom anywhere, drags parameters (Julia seed, Lorenz sigma, rho, beta) and watches sensitivity to initial conditions as two nearly identical trajectories diverge. Era styling of an 80s workstation or plotter printout.

scenes.title: PC demoscene intro
scenes.blurb: A 1990s PC demo: plasma, tunnel, rotozoomer and scroller in 320x200 VGA, synced to a four-channel tracker tune.
scenes.fits: demoscene, real-time graphics, tracker music, VGA, size-coding, 1990s PC culture
scenes.brief: A 320x200 256-colour VGA screen scaled up with a subtle CRT: classic real-time effects (plasma, tunnel, rotozoomer, vector bobs, fire) cycling in parts with fades, a sine scroller of original text, and an original four-channel tracker-style tune synthesized in WebAudio when Sound is on (show pattern rows scrolling in a tracker panel). The viewer can switch effects, change the palette and tweak parameters. Never reproduce a real demo.

scenes.title: CAVE virtual reality room
scenes.blurb: Stand in a cube of projected walls: the image bends to your head position, the way the 1991 CAVE turned a room into a world.
scenes.fits: virtual reality, immersive environments, projection, head tracking, 1990s art and science
scenes.brief: Seen from just behind a visitor, a cubic room whose walls and floor carry an off-axis projection of an original virtual world (early 90s flat-shaded polygons); moving the pointer moves the tracked head and every wall re-projects in perspective (the core CAVE idea made visible), with a toggle to see the room from outside showing the projectors and frusta. The viewer can walk the world with keys or a wand. Credit Carolina Cruz-Neira first in any label.

scenes.title: Interactive evolution
scenes.blurb: A grid of images grown from random formulas; pick the ones you like and the next generation breeds from them.
scenes.fits: interactive evolution, genetic programming, aesthetic selection, artificial life, evolutionary art
scenes.brief: A 3x3 or 4x4 grid of images each rendered on the GPU from a random symbolic expression tree (sin, cos, noise, abs, mix over x, y, r, theta); the viewer clicks favourites and the next generation mutates and crosses them, with a family tree and the expression shown for the selected image. Original expressions only; never mimic a specific artist’s forms.

scenes.title: Flash authoring stage
scenes.blurb: A late-90s authoring stage: a timeline of keyframes, tweened symbols and a script that makes the page react to the mouse.
scenes.fits: Flash, web animation, interactive design, vector animation, 1990s and 2000s web art
scenes.brief: A generic late-90s vector-animation authoring tool (no Macromedia or Adobe branding): stage, layered timeline with keyframes and motion tweens, a symbol library, and an actions panel with an original ActionScript-like snippet; the movie plays in a preview window with mouse-reactive vector motion (easing, onion skin toggle). The viewer drags keyframes, edits a number in the script and scrubs the timeline.

scenes.title: Emergence from simple rules
scenes.blurb: Cells, ants, flocks and slime: a handful of local rules grow patterns no one drew.
scenes.fits: artificial life, cellular automata, agent-based systems, emergence, complexity, generative systems
scenes.brief: One GPU world that switches between rule systems: Game of Life (drawable cells), Langton’s ant, boids flocking, reaction-diffusion (Gray-Scott) and a Physarum-style agent trail network; each shows its rule in one plain line. The viewer draws seeds, changes one parameter and watches the pattern reorganise. Distinct visual identity per rule, sharing one clean scientific-instrument frame.

scenes.title: Language model, trained live
scenes.blurb: A small neural network learns to write by reading, letter by letter, in your browser, and its guesses sharpen as it trains.
scenes.fits: language models, neural text generation, machine learning, generative writing, AI
scenes.brief: A real character-level model (a small RNN or GRU or a tiny transformer) trained live in a Web Worker on a bundled public-domain corpus the viewer can switch (or paste their own text); samples print every few hundred steps and visibly improve from noise to words to phrases; show the next-character probability bars and a temperature slider. Honest labelling: trained live, tiny model, no pretrained weights.

scenes.title: Protocol art contract
scenes.blurb: A simulated on-chain contract whose state is the artwork: votes, deposits and time change the piece, block by block.
scenes.fits: protocol art, DAOs, smart contracts, autonomous systems, blockchain art, governance
scenes.brief: A simulated contract state machine visualised as the artwork: members deposit, propose and vote; proposals pass or fail by quorum; the treasury and rules change; a generative image re-renders from the contract state each block. The viewer joins as a simulated member, proposes a change to one visual parameter and votes; every transaction is labelled simulated, no wallet. Original, not any real DAO or artwork.
